'''''Echeveria gibbiflora''''' is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Crassulaceae]].<ref name=cbg>{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagobotanic.org/plantcollections/plantfinder/echeveria_gibbiflora--echeveria|website=chicagobotanic.org |title=Echeveria gibbiflora|publisher=[[Chicago Botanic Garden]]}}</ref><ref name=cordero2016/><ref name=merc2013>{{cite web |url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2013/09/26/ruths-tips-echeveria-mauna-loa-an-unusual-beauty/|website=mercurynews.com|title=Ruth's Tips: Echeveria 'Mauna Loa' an unusual beauty|publisher=[[The Mercury News]]|date=26 September 2013|accessdate=25 April 2019}}</ref> It was described by Swiss [[botanist]] [[Augustin Pyramus de Candolle]] in 1828. It occurs in Mexico and Guatemala.<ref name=crass/>

==Description==
''Echeveria gibbiflora'' is a large species of ''[[Echeveria]]'',<ref name=cbg/><ref name=crass/> producing rosettes of 15 leaves, a tall flowering stem up to {{convert|1|m}} in height, and an average of 160 flower buds.<ref name=parra1998>{{cite journal|author=Parra-Tabla, V.|author2=Vargas, C. F.|author3=Eguiarte, L. E.|title=Is Echeveria gibbiflora (Crassulaceae) fecundity limited by pollen availability? An experimental study|journal=Functional Ecology|date=August 1998|volume=12|issue=4|pages=591–595 |doi=10.1046/j.1365-2435.1998.00229.x|issn=0269-8463|doi-access=free}}</ref> The red, tubular flowers are about {{convert|2.5|cm}} long with 10 [[stamen]]s and 5 [[style (botany)|styles]].<ref name=parra1998/><ref name=parra1993>{{cite journal|author=Parra, Victor|author2=Vargas, C. Fabian|author3=Eguiarte, Luis E.|title=Reproductive biology, pollen and seed dispersal, and neighborhood size in the hummingbird-pollinated ''Echeveria gibbiflora'' (Crassulaceae)|journal=American Journal of Botany |date=February 1993|volume=80|issue=2|pages=153–159|doi=10.1002/j.1537-2197.1993.tb13783.x}}</ref> It flowers between September and January.<ref name=cbg/><ref name=parra1998/> The dry fruits each produce approximately 200 small seeds.<ref name=parra1998/>

==Ecology==
Each flower is open for between 7–8 days and is visited by nectar-seeking [[broad-billed hummingbird]]s (''Cynanthus latirostris'').<ref name=parra1993/> The [[American bushtit]] (''Psaltriparus minimus'') has been documented foraging for [[aphid]]s that occur among the flowers.<ref name=parra1993/>

==Uses==
''Echeveria gibbiflora'' has been used in Mexican [[folk medicine]] as a [[contraceptive]], as a vaginal postcoital rinse.<ref name=delgado1999>{{cite journal|author=Delgado, N. M.|author2=Taboada Ramirez, J.|author3=Ortega Hernández, A.|author4=Merchant-Larios, H.|author5=Sánchez-Vázqueź, M. L.|author6=Ramirez, G.|author7=Reyes, R.|title=Effects of a purified fraction from Echeveria gibbiflora aqueous crude extract on guinea-pig spermatozoa |journal=Phytotherapy Research|year=1999|volume=13|issue=1|pages=46–49|doi=10.1002/(SICI)1099-1573(199902)13:1<46::AID-PTR373>3.0.CO;2-S|pmid=10189950|issn=0951-418X|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=cordero2016>{{cite journal|author=Cordero-Martinez, Joaquín|author2=Aguirre-Alvarado, Charmina|author3=Guzmán-Soriano, Jessica Gabriela|author4=Sánchez-Arroyo, Cinthia Erika|author5=Flores-Alonso, Juan Carlos|author6=Rodríguez-Páez, Lorena|title=Effects of aqueous crude extract of Echeveria gibbiflora on mouse sperm function|journal=Systems Biology in Reproductive Medicine|date=27 July 2016|volume=62|issue=5|pages=343–52|doi=10.1080/19396368.2016.1203044|pmid=27463087|doi-access=free}}</ref>

Cultivars include ''E. gibbiflora'' 'Carunculata' (also spelled 'Caronculata'),<ref>{{cite web|title=''Echeveria gibbiflora'' 'Caronculata' De Smet|url=http://www.crassulaceae.ch/de/artikel?akID=48&aaID=4&aiID=G&aID=3150|website=www.crassulaceae.ch |publisher=International Crassulaceae Network|accessdate=2018-11-07|language=de}}</ref> ''E. gibbiflora'' 'Metallica', and ''E. gibbiflora'' 'Violescens'.<ref name=eggli2012>{{cite book|author=Eggli, Urs|title=Illustrated Handbook of Succulent Plants: Crassulaceae|year=2012|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=9783642558740}}</ref>
